page: Vultr voc-g-96c-256gb-1280s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 2.67 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the server is equipped with a 1280 GB NVMe SSD, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark data highlights strong multi-threaded capabilities alongside moderate single-core performance. In multi-core processing, the server achieves a top-tier stress-ng multi-core score of 213,580.47 and a strong PassMark CPU score of 81,703.97. The AMD EPYC processor demonstrates top-tier performance in PassMark extended instructions and encryption tests. Single-threaded performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the average tier and single-threaded gzip compression registering in the weak tier. Memory performance is mixed; while small-block cached read-only memory bandwidth reaches a top-tier 8,120.31 GB/sec, large-block uncached read and write bandwidths remain in the average tier.

From a resource density perspective, the server offers high compute density with its 96 dedicated vCPUs, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for parallelized workloads that do not require massive memory-to-CPU ratios. It is well-suited for highly parallel tasks such as multi-threaded decompression, where it achieves a strong bzip3 multi-threaded decompression rate of 439.79 GB/sec. Other appropriate workloads include high-throughput Redis deployments, which perform at a strong rate of 101.76 million SET operations per second, as well as static web serving, database operations, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.

Benchmarks indicate top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 213,580.47, and top-tier results in cryptographic and extended instruction tests. This server is qualitatively cost-efficient for high-density parallel computing, making it suitable for multi-threaded decompression, Redis key-value stores, static web serving, and database operations.
